### BoK Gate check (v3 — MCORCH Master Execution Protocol)

For each BoK suite in `docs/bok/<slug>/`, verify completeness:
```bash
for slug in $(ls docs/bok/ 2>/dev/null); do
  if [ "$slug" = "security" ]; then
    required_sec=(00-deepsearch-blueprint 01-brd-security 02-srs-secure-spec 03-sdd-hardening-architecture 04-fmea-security)
    missing=()
    for doc in "${required_sec[@]}"; do
      [ -f "docs/bok/security/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
    done
    [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ security — BoK complete (ciso-4-artifact)" || echo "⚠️ security — missing: ${missing[*]}"
    continue
  fi
  required=(00-index 01-mrd 02-brd 03-prd 04-frd 05-sdd 06-data-model 07-process-flow 08-quality-metrics)
  missing=()
  for doc in "${required[@]}"; do
    [ -f "docs/bok/$slug/$doc.md" ] || missing+=("$doc")
  done
  [ ${#missing[@]} -eq 0 ] && echo "✅ $slug — BoK complete" || echo "⚠️ $slug — missing: ${missing[*]}"
done
```

## Rules

- **TypeScript errors → report immediately.** If there are TS errors, list them under ALERTAS. Do not start implementing new features until errors are resolved (unless the user explicitly asks to proceed despite errors).
- **Unhealthy containers → report with triage.** Suggest the fix command if known (e.g., `docker compose restart mcorch-vector-engine` for chroma).
- **Uncommitted changes → describe, do not commit.** Only describe what exists in the working tree; committing is the user's call.
- **Keep the brief tight.** No padding. No repetition of CLAUDE.md architecture. The user already knows the architecture — they need the delta: what changed, what's broken, what's next.
- **Pending Actions priority order:** CRITICAL (before first client) > NON-CRITICAL > Phase Zeta > Core v3 > Epsilon v9.
- **Knowledge Mesh numbers:** use `GraphRAG State` section from HANDOFF.md as the source. Do not invent counts.

> === gen-user-jwt.ts uso ===
> #!/usr/bin/env bun
> /**
>  * Mint a REAL user access_token (JWT) for authenticated edge-fn calls in QA — without a browser or raw password.
>  * Admin generateLink (magiclink) → verifyOtp(token_hash) → session.access_token. Per-user, reproducible.
>  * Pattern extends gen-magiclink.ts (v6.20.4). The token is one-time and ~1h-lived; mint right before use.
>  *
>  * Usage: bun run scripts/qa/gen-user-jwt.ts <email>
>  *   → prints the access_token on stdout (nothing else), or an error on stderr + exit 1.
>  *   e.g. TOKEN=$(bun run scripts/qa/gen-user-jwt.ts gabrielcall@gmail.com)
>  */
> import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
> 
> const URL = process.env.SUPABASE_URL ?? process.env.VITE_SUPABASE_URL!;
> const SVC = (process.env.SB_SECRET_KEY ?? process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY)!;
> const ANON = (process.env.SB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? process.env.SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? process.env.VITE_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY)!;
> const email = process.argv[2];
> if (!URL || !SVC || !ANON || !email) {
>   console.error('Usage: gen-user-jwt.ts <email>  (needs SUPABASE_URL + SB_SECRET_KEY + SB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY)');
>   process.exit(1);
> }
> 
> const admin = createClient(URL, SVC, { auth: { persistSession: false } });
> const anon = createClient(URL, ANON, { auth: { persistSession: false } });
> 
> const { data, error } = await admin.auth.admin.generateLink({ type: 'magiclink', email });
> if (error || !data.properties?.hashed_token) {
>   console.error('generateLink error:', error?.message ?? 'no hashed_token');
>   process.exit(1);
> }
> const tokenHash = data.properties.hashed_token;
> 
> let accessToken: string | null = null;
> for (const type of ['magiclink', 'email'] as const) {
>   const { data: sess, error: vErr } = await anon.auth.verifyOtp({ token_hash: tokenHash, type });
>   if (!vErr && sess?.session?.access_token) { accessToken = sess.session.access_token; break; }
> }
> if (!accessToken) { console.error('verifyOtp failed for both magiclink/email types'); process.exit(1); }
> console.log(accessToken);
> ...
> === procura o email do User 0 p/ minter ===
> ```

## 🤖 Claude *(02:11:20)*

Segurança confirmada: `scheduled_posts` INSERT tem `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id)` → `post.user_id` é server-trusted (RLS). `publish-channel-variant` é o molde exato de enqueue. Meu `publish-space-asset` espelha: user-JWT → getUser → service-role resolve asset owner-scoped → upsert variant → enqueue com `metadata.reshape.space_publish_variant_id`. Agora leio o schema exato de `creative_assets` + o padrão completo do nó WordPress (registry/tipo/componente/inspector) + enum `social_platform` para clonar com fidelidade.

## 🤖 Claude *(02:12:41)*

Tenho tudo. Refinamento de segurança importante que farei vs. o sketch do ADR: a UNIQUE do sketch era `(node_run_id, channel, surface)`, mas `node_run_id` é um id de nó do canvas (string client-supplied, não UUID) → incluí-lo numa UNIQUE global arriscaria **colisão cross-tenant** (DoS/leak). Vou ancorar em `UNIQUE(user_id, source_asset_id, channel, surface)` — tenant-scoped e idempotente por intenção de publicação. Começo pelo SOP (Lei 2 — antes do código).

Refinamento material sobre o sketch (Lei 1).\n- **`asset_status` default `'ready'`:** o asset do Spaces j\u00e1 existe (\u2260 pillar, onde o render \u00e9 async). Sem estados de render pendente.\n"

The caption is the caller's OWN content going to the\n// caller's OWN social account \u2014 no cross-tenant trust boundary \u2014 but we still shape it to avoid storing arbitrary junk.\nfunction sanitizeNativeText(raw: unknown): Record<string, unknown> {\n  const src = (raw && typeof raw === \"object\") ? raw as Record<string, unknown> : {};\n  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};\n  for (const k of [\"caption\", \"title\", \"description\", \"body\", \"link\"]) {\n    if (typeof src[k] === \"string\") out[k] = (src[k] as string).slice(0, 5000);\n  }\n  if (Array.isArray(src.tweets)) {\n    out.tweets = (src.tweets as unknown[]).filter((t) => typeof t === \"string\").slice(0, 25).map((t) => (t as string).slice(0, 5000));\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n\nDeno.serve(async (req) => {\n  if (req.method === \"OPTIONS\") return new Response(\"ok\", { headers: corsHeaders });\n\n  const json = (status: number, body: unknown) =>\n    new Response(JSON.stringify(body), { status, headers: { ...corsHeaders, \"Content-Type\": \"application/json\" } });\n\n  try {\n    const authHeader = req.headers.get(\"Authorization\");\n    if (!authHeader?.startsWith(\"Bearer \")) return json(401, { error: \"Unauthorized\" });\n\n    // Re-verify the caller (gateway already validated the JWT signature).\n    const userClient = createClient(\n      Deno.env.get(\"SUPABASE_URL\")!,\n      (Deno.env.get(\"SB_PUBLISHABLE_KEY\") ?? \"video\" : asset.kind === \"image\" ? \"image\" : \"none\";\n\n    const nativeText = sanitizeNativeText(body.native_text);\n    const nodeRunId = typeof body.node_run_id === \"string\" ? body.node_run_id.slice(0, 200) : null;\n    const spaceId = typeof body.space_id === \"string\" ? body.space_id : null;\n\n    // \u2500\u2500 Upsert the variant (idempotent on user_id, source_asset_id, channel, surface). status/scheduled_post_id are\n    //    NOT in the payload \u2192 on conflict they are NOT downgraded (a re-call never un-schedules a scheduled variant). \u2500\u2500\n    const { data: variant, error: upErr } = await admin.from(\"space_publish_variants\")\n      .upsert({\n        user_id: user.id,\n        space_id: spaceId,\n        node_run_id: nodeRunId,\n        source_asset_id: asset.id,\n        channel,\n        surface,\n        platform,\n        native_text: nativeText,\n        asset_kind: assetKind,\n        asset_bucket: asset.storage_bucket,   // SERVER-TRUSTED (from the owner row), never from the client\n        asset_key: asset.storage_key,\n        asset_status: \"ready\",\n      }, { onConflict: \"user_id,source_asset_id,channel,surface\" })\n      .select(\"id, status, scheduled_post_id, platform\").single();\n    if (upErr || !variant) return json(500, { error: \"upsert_failed\", detail: upErr?.message });\n\n    // \u2500\u2500 Draft mode (default): variant created/refreshed, publishable later. \u2500\u2500\n    if (!wantPublish) {\n      return json(200, { ok: true, space_publish_variant_id: variant.id, status: variant.status, platform: variant.platform });\n    }\n\n    // \u2500\u2500 Publish mode: enqueue into scheduled_posts (auto-publish resolves the asset owner-scoped from the variant). \u2500\u2500\n    if (!variant.platform) {\n      return json(422, { error: \"surface_not_publishable\", action: \"Este canal/superf\u00edcie n\u00e3o mapeia para uma rede public\u00e1vel.\" });\n    }\n    if (variant.scheduled_post_id || variant.status === \"scheduled\" || variant.status === \"published\") {\n      return json(409, { error: \"already_enqueued\", scheduled_post_id: variant.scheduled_post_id });\n    }\n\n    const text = typeof nativeText.caption === \"string\" ? > 4	/**
> 5	 * Durable asset-URL resolution for a private-bucket world (SOP: docs/processes/[[private-bucket-asset-signing|private-bucket-asset-signing]].md).
> 6	 *
> 7	 * The storage buckets that hold creative media (canvas-assets, generated-images, video-studio-assets, …) are
> 8	 * PRIVATE + owner-scoped. A `/object/public/<bucket>/…` URL to a private bucket GETs HTTP 400, and a signed URL
> 9	 * expires. So NOTHING durable should be a baked URL: display must RE-RESOLVE on every render — extract (bucket,
> 10	 * key) from whatever URL is stored (dead-public OR expired-signed) and mint a FRESH signed URL. The owner-scoped
> 11	 * storage SELECT policies (migration 20260703030000) let the owner — and only the owner — sign their own objects.
> 12	 */
> 13	
> 14	// The ONLY buckets readable by a bare public URL (published posts / IG / WordPress need a durable public video_url).
> 15	// Everything else is private → signed URL. Keyed off the BUCKET (server truth), never a possibly-stale is_public flag.
> 16	const PUBLIC_BUCKETS = new Set<string>(["generated-videos"]);
> 17	
> 18	const SIGNED_TTL_SECONDS = 3600; // 1h — display re-signs on every mount, so a short TTL is both safe and enough.
> 19	
> 20	/** Parse a Supabase Storage URL — public `/object/public/<bucket>/<key>` or signed `/object/sign/<bucket>/<key>?token=`
> 21	 *  — into { bucket, key }. Returns null for anything else (external provider URL, data:/blob: URI, plain string). */
> 22	export function parseStorageRef(url: string): { bucket: string; key: string } | null {
> 23	  const m = url.match(/\/storage\/v1\/object\/(?:public|sign)\/([^/]+)\/([^?]+)/);
> 24	  if (!m) return null;
> 25	  return { bucket: decodeURIComponent(m[1]), key: decodeURIComponent(m[2]) };
> 26	}
> 27	
> 28	/** Sign (private) or public-URL (public bucket) a concrete storage ref. Falls back to `fallback` on sign failure. */
> 29	export async function signStorageRef(
> 30	  bucket: string,
> 31	  key: string,
> 32	  fallback: string | null = null,
> 33	): Promise<string | null> {
> 34	  if (PUBLIC_BUCKETS.has(bucket)) {
> 35	    return supabase.storage.from(bucket).getPublicUrl(key).data.publicUrl;
> 36	  }
> 37	  const { data } = await supabase.storage.from(bucket).createSignedUrl(key, SIGNED_TTL_SECONDS);
> 38	  return data?.signedUrl ?? fallback;
> 39	}
> 40	
> 41	/**
> 42	 * Resolve a viewable URL for a stored media value. Re-resolves durably:
> 43	 * - a full Supabase storage URL (public OR expired-signed) → fresh signed / public URL for its bucket
> 44	 * - a non-storage value (external provider URL, data:/blob: URI, undefined) → returned unchanged
> 45	 */
> 46	export async function toDisplayUrl(input: string | null | undefined): Promise<string | null> {
> 47	  if (!input) return null;
> 48	  const ref = parseStorageRef(input);
> 49	  if (!ref) return input; // external / data: / blob: — not ours to sign
> 50	  return signStorageRef(ref.bucket, ref.key, input);
> 51	}
> 52	
> 53	/** React hook: resolves a stored media value to a viewable URL, cached + auto-refreshed before the signed TTL. */
> 54	export function useDisplayUrl(input: string | null | undefined): string | null {
> 55	  const { data } = useQuery({
> 56	    queryKey: ["display-url", input],
> 57	    enabled: !!input,
> 58	    // Refresh comfortably before the signed URL expires so a long-open tab never shows a stale 400.
> 59	    staleTime: (SIGNED_TTL_SECONDS - 300) * 1000,

> 62	  });

Channel naming follows channel_profiles SPEC ('twitter_x').\n\nexport interface PublishDestination {\n  id: string;\n  label: string;\n  channel: string;\n  surface: string;\n  platform: \"instagram\" | \"tiktok\" | \"youtube\" | \"facebook\" | \"linkedin\" | \"pinterest\" | \"twitter\";\n  kind: \"video\" | \"image\" | \"any\";\n}\n\nexport const PUBLISH_DESTINATIONS: PublishDestination[] = [\n  { id: \"instagram_reels\", label: \"Instagram Reels\", channel: \"instagram\", surface: \"reels\", platform: \"instagram\", kind: \"video\" },\n  { id: \"instagram_feed\",  label: \"Instagram Feed\",  channel: \"instagram\", surface: \"feed\",  platform: \"instagram\", kind: \"image\" },\n  { id: \"tiktok\",          label: \"TikTok\",          channel: \"tiktok\",    surface: \"video\", platform: \"tiktok\",    kind: \"video\" },\n  { id: \"youtube_shorts\",  label: \"YouTube Shorts\",  channel: \"youtube\",   surface: \"shorts\", platform: \"youtube\",  kind: \"video\" },\n  { id: \"facebook_feed\",   label: \"Facebook\",        channel: \"facebook\",  surface: \"feed\",  platform: \"facebook\",  kind: \"any\" },\n  { id: \"linkedin_feed\",   label: \"LinkedIn\",        channel: \"linkedin\",  surface: \"feed\",  platform: \"linkedin\",  kind: \"any\" },\n  { id: \"pinterest_pin\",   label: \"Pinterest\",       channel: \"pinterest\", surface: \"pin\",   platform: \"pinterest\", kind: \"image\" },\n  { id: \"twitter_post\",    label: \"X (Twitter)\",     channel: \"twitter_x\", surface: \"post\",  platform: \"twitter\",   kind: \"any\" },\n];\n\nexport function getPublishDestination(id: string): PublishDestination {\n  return PUBLISH_DESTINATIONS.find((d) => d.id === id) ?? PUBLISH_DESTINATIONS[0];\n}\n"
}

> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:53:### Pilar I — Assembler multi-cena (a camada de cola que falta)
> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:57:- **Stage 1 — cena auto-contida, duração dirigida pelo áudio.** A narração é a fonte de verdade da duração da cena (padrão faceless-channel: VO primeiro, visual timado a ela — [github.com/SaarD00/AI-Youtube-Shorts-Generator](https://github.com/SaarD00/AI-Youtube-Shorts-Generator), verificado que existe e sincroniza duração à narração). Normalize cada clipe a params canônicos (resolução fixa, CFR fixo, `yuv420p`, `setsar=1`, timebase fixo), pad/trim video+áudio à duração exata da narração, resample toda narração a 48000 Hz estéreo, mux. Legendas locais queimadas **aqui** (ver Pilar IV) mantêm o join final em `-c copy`.
> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:58:- **Stage 2 — concat demuxer, stream-copy.** Como Stage 1 igualou codecs/resolução/fps/timebase, o concat demuxer junta com `-c copy` — sem re-encode, sem perda, determinístico. O demuxer exige "same codecs, same time base" e reescreve timestamps para "the first file starts at 0 and each next file starts where the previous one finishes" ([ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-formats.html)). **Este é o spine default.**
> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:59:- **Transições (xfade) são opt-in re-encode, NÃO o spine.** `xfade` força re-encode completo, exige CFR + resolução/pixfmt/fps/timebase idênticos, e `offset` calculado à mão por transição ([ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html); corroborado [ayosec mirror](https://ayosec.github.io/ffmpeg-filters-docs/8.0/Filters/Video/xfade.html)). **Fragilidade concreta verificada:** o guia FFmpegLab publica `offset=9` para o 2º corte (clipes 5s, T=1s), mas o valor **overlap-correto** é **8** (`offset_k = (Σ Dᵢ) − k·T`); `offset=9` deixa zero sobreposição. Essa aritmética off-by-T é razão material para preferir render-por-cena-com-duração-exata + concat-demuxer, que **elimina** o cálculo de offset.
> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:67:| **Editly** | **MIT** ([npmjs](https://www.npmjs.com/package/editly)) | Drop-in declarativo mais próximo; mas é wrapper FFmpeg — worker próprio dá mais controle de determinismo. |
> docs/bok/youtube-studio/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md:68:| **ffmpeg-python** | **Apache-2.0** ([pypi](https://pypi.org/project/ffmpeg-python/)) | Bom modelo, runtime errado (MCORCH é Deno/TS). |

"Sem obrigação em uso server-side (SaaS ≠ distribuição)" é **juízo de engenharia**, não termo citado — vira OTD (§7).

O `composition` jsonb carrega a **cut-spec data-driven** (lista `{in, out, reframe, caption_source}` por clipe \u2014 **n\u00e3o cravada**, filosofia `mapa_transicoes.py` do GabrielAI: cortes de dado, n\u00e3o de texto). Opera\u00e7\u00f5es FFmpeg (can\u00f4nicas, cf. `ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg-filters.html` j\u00e1 citado no youtube-studio blueprint):\n- **corte** 1 longo \u2192 N: `-ss <in> -to <out>` por clipe (stream-accurate);\n- **reframe 16:9\u21929:16 subject-safe:** `crop=ih*9/16:ih:(iw-ih*9/16)/2:0,scale=1080:1920` (center default; **OTD-VR-002:** crop din\u00e2mico subject-aware = fatia posterior, MVP=center-safe);\n- **queima de legenda:** `subtitles=<srt>` (filtro `subtitles`, do SRT ingerido ou texto por clipe) \u2014 \u2260 GabrielAI (que envia SRT como faixa no MASTER; aqui os SHORTS queimam, contexto social distinto);\n- **sa\u00edda:** clipes MP4 9:16 registrados `creative_assets` `kind='video'` `source_module='external'` (derivado, `parent_asset_id`=master) \u2192 **o sink `publish-space-asset` j\u00e1 sabe consumir**.\n\n### Pilar III \u2014 CARROSSEL de Instagram \u00b7 Fatia 3\nExtrai key-frames do master (`ffmpeg -ss <t> -frames:v 1`) em timestamps (dos `atos[]`/cap\u00edtulos), comp\u00f5e slides via **`render-core.ts`** (HTML\u2192PNG existente, aceita `images[]`): quadro + cita\u00e7\u00e3o/legenda, **1080\u00d71350** (4:5). Estende a branch IG do `publish-social` para **`media_type=CAROUSEL`** (children `image_url`+`is_carousel_item=true`, \u226410 \u2192 parent \u2192 `media_publish`). Reusa a superf\u00edcie `carousel` do `channel_profiles` (hoje LinkedIn/PDF; **OTD-VR-003:** adicionar surface IG-carousel image-set, que o pr\u00f3prio migration `20260628120000:7` j\u00e1 marcou \"later slice\").\n\n### Pilar IV \u2014 MAPEADOR de metadados \u00b7 Fatia 4\nL\u00ea os metadados estruturados do epis\u00f3dio (schema `episodios/epNN.json`) e emite: (a) a **legenda nativa por plataforma** e (b) o **corpo HTML do WordPress** (v\u00eddeo embedado + **fontes creditadas** de `creditos.blocos[]` \u2014 n\u00e3o perder cap\u00edtulos/fontes). **OTD-VR-004:** o `reshape-pillar` \u00e9 pillar-coupled (`pillar_run_id`+`pillar_atoms`); o mapeador reusa a **gram\u00e1tica `field_map` / voicing** do `channel_profiles.transform_recipe` mas alimentada pelo metadado do epis\u00f3dio (n\u00e3o por um pillar_run) \u2014 a decis\u00e3o exata (adaptar reshape-pillar vs. mapper leve dedicado) \u00e9 FRD da Fatia 4.\n\n### Pilar V \u2014 FIAR na distribui\u00e7\u00e3o existente \u00b7 Fatia 5\nClipes/carross\u00e9is/post escoam por: **`publish-space-asset`\u2192`space_publish_variants`\u2192`auto-publish`\u2192`publish-social`** (TikTok/YT/IG) + **`publish-wordpress`**. Disclosure sint\u00e9tica (is_aigc/containsSyntheticMedia) **hard-coded preservada**. **Gate externo honesto (n\u00e3o c\u00f3digo):** alcance p\u00fablico depende de auditoria de app \u2014 TikTok for\u00e7a `SELF_ONLY`, YouTube pode for\u00e7ar privado pr\u00e9-audit (`publish-social:290-297,388`). A\u00e7\u00e3o do Sovereign.\n\n## 4. **NO FINDINGS** (no real vulnerability at confidence ≥7).

### Verification of the "list-only" premise
Diff of `20260712120000` RPC body (lines 19-90) against the sealed reunion `20260710170000` (lines 17-88), after injecting `'external'` into the reunion's IN-list, is empty except for one comment line. The `CHECK` constraint and the `p_source_module` guard each gain exactly one UNION member (`'external'`); INSERT column list, `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id` anti-hijack guard, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `SET search_path = ''`, and the `REVOKE ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` / `GRANT ... TO service_role` are byte-identical. Money-path untouched. Confirmed list-only. (confidence 10)

### Point-by-point trace

**Cross-tenant object registration via the `${user.id}/` guard** (`ingest-external-asset/index.ts:65`) — Closed. `user` comes from `getUser()` (server-verified JWT, `:47-48`), and `storageKey` must `startsWith(\`${user.id}/\`)`. UUIDs are fixed-length (36 chars), so no user's UUID prefix is ever a prefix of another's path → no prefix collision. A forged `..` key (`${attacker.id}/../{victim}/x.mp4`) still literally starts with the attacker's own UUID, so it passes, but the row is stored with `user_id = attacker` and a literal (non-normalized) key; Supabase/S3 treats keys as opaque strings (no filesystem `..` collapse), so it does not alias the victim's real object. And this seam never reads/signs the object — the service-role `admin` client is used only for the RPC insert and a static `infra_health_logs` write (`:86-103`). No cross-tenant read materializes in Fatia 1. (confidence 9)

**Row-hijack via UNIQUE (bucket,key)** — Doubly closed: an attacker can never produce a `(bucket,key)` colliding with a victim's row (victim's key carries the victim's UUID prefix), and even if they could, `ON CONFLICT ... WHERE public.creative_assets.user_id = EXCLUDED.user_id` (`:82`) suppresses the UPDATE, `v_id` returns NULL, and the edge returns 500 (`:101`). (confidence 9)

**jsonb / SRT injection &amp; stored XSS firing now** — `p_metadata` is passed as a JS object through `supabase.rpc` (parameterized jsonb; `metadata || EXCLUDED.metadata` is jsonb concat — no SQL injection). Size-gated `episode`/`srt` land in `metadata` on a row that is owner-only: `p_org_id` is never passed (defaults NULL), so `creative_assets` SELECT (own-or-org) resolves to own-only — no cross-tenant reader. No HTML sink is added in this fatia. Excluded self-XSS aside, no live vector. (confidence 9)

**Direct `authenticated` RPC call** — `REVOKE ALL ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` + `GRANT EXECUTE ... TO service_role` (`:89-90`). A user JWT cannot invoke the RPC directly; the only path forces `p_user_id = user.id` from the verified token — `user_id` is unforgeable. (confidence 10)

**501 YouTube fallback leak** (`:54-60`) — Returns only a static PT-BR message + `OTD-VR-001` marker. No secrets/internal state. (confidence 10)

**MAX_META / MAX_SRT bypass (non-DoS)** — `sizedString`/`sizedObject` measure exact UTF-8 bytes via `Blob`; oversized input is dropped to the `?? {}` / skipped default, never stored oversized. No integrity bypass. (confidence 9)

### Forward-looking note (below threshold — NOT a Fatia-1 vuln, do not gate on this)
`storage_bucket` is client-controlled and **not** validated (`:63` accepts any string, guard only checks `storage_key` prefix). Harmless now because the key is still pinned to the caller's own UUID namespace and nothing in this fatia reads the object. But the Fatia 2 segmentation worker (service-role) will `download`/sign `(storage_bucket, storage_key)` from this row. > 203	/** One drain pass: claim + render every queued hyperframes render. Returns count processed. */
> 204	async function drainOnce(): Promise<number> {
> 205	  // Reap renders stuck in 'running' past the timeout (dead worker) → back to queued for re-claim.
> 206	  const cutoff = new Date(Date.now() - RUNNING_TIMEOUT_MS).toISOString();
> 207	  await supabase.from('video_renders')
> 208	    .update({ state: 'queued' })
> 209	    .eq('engine', 'hyperframes').eq('state', 'running').lt('updated_at', cutoff)
> 210	    .then(() => {}, () => {});
> 211	
> 212	  const { data: queued, error } = await supabase
> 213	    .from('video_renders')
> 214	    .select('id')
> 215	    .eq('engine', 'hyperframes').eq('state', 'queued')
> 216	    .order('created_at', { ascending: true })
> 217	    .limit(10);
> 218	  if (error || !queued?.length) return 0;
> 219	
> 220	  let n = 0;
> 221	  for (const q of queued) {
> 222	    const row = await claim(q.id);
> 223	    if (!row) continue; // already claimed by another worker
> 224	    await processRender(row as any);
> 225	    n++;
> 226	  }
> 227	  return n;
> 228	}
> 229	
> 230	async function main() {
> 231	  const once = process.argv.includes('--once');
> 232	  if (once) {
> 233	    const n = await drainOnce();
> 234	    console.log(`drained ${n} render(s)`);
> 235	    process.exit(0);
> 236	  }
> 237	  console.log('🎬 video-bridge running — polling video_renders (engine=hyperframes, queued)...');
> 238	  await logHealth('healthy', 'worker_started');
> 239	  // eslint-disable-next-line no-constant-condition
> 240	  while (true) {
> 241	    try {
> 242	      await drainOnce();
> 243	    } catch (e) {
> 244	      console.error('poll cycle error:', e);
> 245	      await logHealth('degraded', 'poll_error', { error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) });
> 246	    }
> 247	    await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, POLL_MS));
> 248	  }
> 249	}
> 250	
> 251	main();
> 252	
> ```

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bun\n/**\n * scripts/video-repurpose/segment-core.ts\n *\n * The FFmpeg core of the video-repurpose engine (Fatia 2): a long 16:9 master + a data-driven cut-spec \u2192\n * N vertical shorts (9:16 or 1:1), reframed subject-safe (center-crop) with an optional burned caption.\n *\n * BoK SSOT: docs/bok/video-repurpose/00-[[deepsearch-blueprint|deepsearch-blueprint]].md \u00a7Pilar II (FR-VR-003/004/005).\n * PROVEN offline 2026-07-12 (Vision QA): a synthetic 16:9 master with ESQ|CENTRO|DIR labels \u2192 the 9:16 center-crop\n * kept CENTRO, dropped the side labels, and burned the caption at the base. Deterministic FFmpeg \u2014 no LLM in the core.\n *\n * Reframe is source-agnostic (expression crop): for a target aspect ar, keep the largest centered rect of that aspect.\n * Caption is written to a per-clip textfile \u2192 drawtext `textfile=` (avoids the `:'%\\` escaping trap of inline text).\n * Cut is re-encoded (`-ss <in> -i -t <dur>`) \u2192 frame-accurate (the reframe re-encodes anyway).\n */\n\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync, existsSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { join } from 'node:path';\n\nconst FONT = '/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf';\n\nexport type Reframe = '9:16' | '1:1';\nexport interface ClipSpec {\n  in_sec: number;\n  out_sec: number;\n  caption?: string;          // burned bottom-center caption (drawtext textfile); omit for none\n  reframe?: Reframe;         // default '9:16'\n}\nexport interface SegmentSpec {\n  sourcePath: string;        // local path to the master MP4\n  clips: ClipSpec[];\n  outDir: string;\n  fps?: number;              // default 30 (CFR)\n}\nexport interface ClipResult {\n  index: number; path: string; width: number; height: number; durationSec: number; bytes: number;\n}\n\nconst TARGET: Record<Reframe, { w: number; h: number; ar: number }> = {\n  '9:16': { w: 1080, h: 1920, ar: 9 / 16 },\n  '1:1': { w: 1080, h: 1080, ar: 1 },\n};\n\nfunction run(cmd: string, args: string[]): Promise<void> {\n  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {\n    const p = spawn(cmd, args, { stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'pipe'] });\n    let err = '';\n    p.stderr.on('data', (d) => { err += d.toString(); });\n    p.on('error', reject);\n    p.on('close', (code) => code === 0 ? resolve() : reject(new Error(`${cmd} exit ${code}: ${err.slice(-500)}`)));\n  });\n}\n\n/** Source-agnostic center-crop to `ar`, then scale to (W,H). Keeps the largest centered rect of the target aspect. */\nfunction reframeChain(ar: number, W: number, H: number): string {\n  // crop w = min(iw, ih*ar); h = min(ih, iw/ar); centered. Expressions are evaluated by FFmpeg per input dims.\n  const cw = `min(iw\\\\,ih*${ar})`;\n  const ch = `min(ih\\\\,iw/${ar})`;\n  return `crop=${cw}:${ch}:(iw-ow)/2:(ih-oh)/2,scale=${W}:${H}:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=${W}:${H},setsar=1`;\n}\n\n/** Cut + reframe + optional caption for ONE clip. Returns the output path. */\nasync function renderClip(spec: SegmentSpec, clip: ClipSpec, index: number): Promise<ClipResult> {\n  const target = TARGET[clip.reframe ?? '9:16'];\n  const fps = spec.fps ?? 30;\n  const dur = Math.max(0.1, clip.out_sec - clip.in_sec);\n  const outPath = join(spec.outDir, `clip_${String(index).padStart(3, '0')}.mp4`);\n\n  let vf = reframeChain(target.ar, target.w, target.h);\n  if (clip.caption && clip.caption.trim()) {\n    // textfile avoids inline-escaping; drawtext reads UTF-8. Bottom-center with a translucent box.\n    const capPath = join(spec.outDir, `cap_${index}.txt`);\n    writeFileSync(capPath, clip.caption.trim());\n    const fontsize = Math.round(target.w * 0.045);\n    vf += `,drawtext=textfile='${capPath}':fontfile=${FONT}:fontsize=${fontsize}:fontcolor=white:` +\n      `box=1:boxcolor=black@0.55:boxborderw=14:x=(w-tw)/2:y=h-th-${Math.round(target.h * 0.08)}`;\n  }\n\n  await run('ffmpeg', [\n    '-y', '-hide_banner', '-loglevel', 'error',\n    '-ss', String(clip.in_sec), '-i', spec.sourcePath, '-t', String(dur),\n    '-vf', vf, '-r', String(fps),\n    '-c:v', 'libx264', '-preset', 'medium', '-pix_fmt', 'yuv420p',\n    '-c:a', 'aac', '-b:a', '128k', '-movflags', '+faststart',\n    outPath,\n  ]);\n\n  const bytes = statSync(outPath).size;\n  return { index, path: outPath, width: target.w, height: target.h, durationSec: dur, bytes };\n}\n\n/** Segment a master into N clips per the cut-spec. Serial (deterministic, memory-safe for a long master). */\nexport async function segmentVideo(spec: SegmentSpec): Promise<ClipResult[]> {\n  if (!existsSync(spec.sourcePath)) throw new Error(`source_not_found: ${spec.sourcePath}`);\n  if (!Array.isArray(spec.clips) || spec.clips.length === 0) throw new Error('cut_spec_empty');\n  mkdirSync(spec.outDir, { recursive: true });\n  const out: ClipResult[] = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i < spec.clips.length; i++) {\n    const c = spec.clips[i];\n    if (!(c.out_sec > c.in_sec) || c.in_sec < 0) throw new Error(`clip_${i}_invalid_range`);\n    out.push(await renderClip(spec, c, i));\n  }\n  return out;\n}\n"
}

Every cross-tenant, injection, and money-mint path I traced closes cleanly. Details below, per your scrutiny checklist.

### Cross-tenant read (FMEA-011) — CLOSED
Trace holds end-to-end:
- Enqueue (`video-repurpose-run/index.ts:70-72`) resolves the source **owner-scoped** — `.eq("id", sourceAssetId).eq("user_id", user.id)` — so a foreign asset id → `maybeSingle()` null → 404 (`:73`). The `.eq user_id` is strictly `auth.uid()`, **not** org-scoped, so even an org co-member cannot repurpose another member's asset.
- The resolved bucket/key is re-validated at enqueue (`:76`): allowlist + `${user.id}/` prefix + no `..`.
- The worker **re-validates the stored composition at read time** (OTD-VR-006, `video-repurpose-bridge.ts:66-69`) against `row.user_id` (server-trusted — written by the seam, never client-set). Download (`:72`) uses service-role (bypasses RLS), so this prefix check is the sole gate — and it is present and fails closed.
- The caller controls only `source_asset_id`; `composition.source.{bucket,key}` is DB-derived, never client-supplied. **Confirmed materially:** `video_renders` has `NO INSERT/UPDATE policy for authenticated ⇒ default-deny` (migration `20260622040000_video_studio_renders_and_assets.sql:15,67`), so a caller cannot forge a row with a foreign `user_id` + matching source prefix. No prefix-confusion (UUID fixed-length; `/` delimiter). No bypass.

### Cross-tenant write — CLOSED
Clips land at `${row.user_id}/repurpose/${renderId}/...` (`bridge.ts:81`); `register_creative_asset` sets `user_id = p_user_id = row.user_id` with `p_is_public=false` (`bridge.ts:85-87`). **Confirmed materially:** `register_creative_asset` is `SECURITY DEFINER`, `REVOKE...FROM PUBLIC,anon,authenticated` / `GRANT...service_role` (migration `20260710170000:87-88`). `row.user_id` unforgeable (same default-deny argument). `renderId` is a DB UUID → unique path, no cross-tenant overwrite despite `upsert:true` (`bridge.ts:83`).

### Command / path injection in FFmpeg — CLOSED
- `spawn('ffmpeg', args[])` array form, no shell (`segment-core.ts:47,80`) → no shell injection.
- The user caption is **written to a per-clip textfile** and consumed via drawtext `textfile='${capPath}'` (`:74,76`) — caption *content* never enters the `-vf` string, so no FFmpeg filter injection. drawtext text-expansion functions (`%{...}`) are arithmetic/metadata only (no file read, no shell); a hostile expansion at worst fails the caller's own clip → self-content DoS (excluded).
- Every path (`outDir`, `capPath`, `outPath`, `clipKey`) derives from `renderId` (DB UUID) + loop index — zero user input → no traversal into the textfile/output paths. `fontfile` is a server constant, not caption-derived.
- Numeric args (`in_sec/out_sec/fps`) are validated at the seam (`:32,62`) and re-checked in core (`:101`); array-passed regardless.

### charged_mco / finalize — CLOSED (no mint)
Seam hardcodes `charged_mco:0` (`:83`); worker `charged = row.charged_mco ?? 0` = 0; success `p_refund:0`, failure `p_refund:charged`=0 (`bridge.ts:108,115`). `finalize_video_render` is service-role-only terminal authority. No positive coin movement on any path.

### Migration is CHECK-list-only — CONFIRMED byte-identical
Prior deployed CHECK per `20260709234000_voice_qwen3_local_engine.sql:35` = `('faceless','hyperframes','qwen3-voice')`. New migration (`20260712130000:13`) = same list **+ 'repurpose'**, nothing else. No RLS/RPC/grant/column change; only a `DROP...IF EXISTS` (by the correct deployed name `video_renders_engine_check`) + re-ADD + COMMENT. Money path untouched.

### 202 / error responses — no meaningful leak
404 is deliberately ambiguous ("não existe ou não é seu", `:73`) → no existence oracle. The one info-disclosure is `detail: insErr?.message` on the 500 enqueue-fail branch (`:92`), but that is a service-role Postgres error string (no cross-tenant data), below the ≥7 bar and in the excluded "hardening" bucket.
